title: Ascendo Sidecar v1
description: Canonical JSON Schema for Ascendo's per-phase sidecar contract (``ascendo/v1``). Native emitters write one sidecar per phase to ``runs/<run-id>/<phase>__<category>.json``; Python readers in the core orchestrator validate against this schema before parsing. Generated from ``core/ascendo/models/sidecar.py`` via ``scripts/export-sidecar-schema.py`` — do not hand-edit. See ADR-0003 for the schema's role in the architecture.

ElevationMethod.description:
How the run process obtained elevated privileges (if at all).

`none` means no elevation was used; the run executed as the invoking
user. `sudo`, `pkexec`, `doas`, and `uac` describe the actual mechanism
when one was used.
ElevationMethod.title: ElevationMethod

HostInfo.description:
Snapshot of the machine state at run start.

Frozen — once captured, never mutated.

os.description: Detected operating system family. Drives adapter selection.

os_version.description: Free-form OS version string. Examples: '24.04 LTS' (Ubuntu), '11 Pro 26200' (Windows), '14.5 (23F79)' (macOS Sonoma).
os_version.title: Os Version

user.description: Username under which the run is executing.
user.title: User

is_elevated.description: True if the run process has effective elevated privileges (root on POSIX, Administrator on Windows).
is_elevated.title: Is Elevated

elevation_method.description: Mechanism used to obtain elevation, if any.

locale.description: BCP-47 locale tag of the user shell, if known. Used for i18n lookups in the orchestrator. Example: 'pl-PL', 'en-US'.
locale.title: Locale

HostInfo.title: HostInfo

Item.description:
One package operation attempted (or skipped, or planned) in this phase.

The same `id` may appear once per phase per run. `current_version` is
pre-apply state; `resolved_version` is post-apply truth; `target_version`
is what the planner intended.

current_version.description: Version installed before this phase (None if not installed).
current_version.title: Current Version

target_version.description: Version the planner intended to install.
target_version.title: Target Version

resolved_version.description: Version actually installed after apply (or what `verify` proved). Distinct from target_version when the source ships a different build than advertised.
resolved_version.title: Resolved Version

exit_code.description: Underlying tool's exit code. e.g. winget's -1978335190.
exit_code.title: Exit Code

duration_ms.description: Wall-clock duration of this item operation, in milliseconds.
duration_ms.title: Duration Ms

evidence.description: Local-version evidence. Set by adapters that need unknown-version suppression (PowerShell-style).

rollback.description: Rollback method for a successful apply. None on check/plan/verify; expected to be set on successful apply.

messages.description: Per-item log lines from the native tool.
messages.title: Messages

Item.title: Item

ItemEvidence.description:
Local-version evidence for unknown-version suppression.

Some package managers (notably winget on certain MSIX packages)
return `Version = Unknown` even though the local install has a
parseable version. The PowerShell adapter records what it can find
via AppX manifest, registry ARP, dpkg, etc. — and the orchestrator
suppresses repeat upgrade offers until the source actually advertises
a newer `Available` version.

All fields are optional; presence indicates the corresponding evidence
was actually gathered.

registry_version.description: Version from Windows registry Add/Remove Programs entry.
registry_version.title: Registry Version

binary_path.description: Absolute path to the resolved binary (for native installers).
binary_path.title: Binary Path

binary_sha256.description: SHA-256 hex of the binary, when checksum verification was performed.
binary_sha256.title: Binary Sha256

note.description: Free-form note explaining why this evidence was gathered.
note.title: Note

ItemEvidence.title: ItemEvidence

ItemRollback.description:
How to undo a successful apply on this item.

Per ADR + threat-model: every apply that succeeds must record a
rollback hint, even if rollback is implemented via system snapshot
(Time Machine / VSS / timeshift) rather than per-package downgrade.

available.description: False means rollback is not possible without a system snapshot.
available.title: Available

method.description: Concrete rollback command, if available. Example: 'winget install --id Microsoft.PowerShell --version 7.6.0' or 'apt install firefox=128.0+build1-0ubuntu0.24.04.1'.
method.title: Method

snapshot_id.description: ID of the pre-apply system snapshot (timeshift snapshot name, VSS shadow copy GUID, Time Machine timestamp). When set, rollback via snapshot is the recommended path.
snapshot_id.title: Snapshot Id

instructions_path.description: Path to a generated markdown file containing human-readable rollback instructions. Default: ~/.ascendo/rollback/<run-id>.md.
instructions_path.title: Instructions Path

ItemRollback.title: ItemRollback

ItemSource.description:
The source/feed an item was discovered through.

Distinct from `Package.category`: a package can have multiple sources
(apt + snap), and `ItemSource.feed` may be more specific than the
category (e.g. category='apt', feed='ubuntu/noble/main' or 'PPA:ondrej/php').

feed.description: Optional sub-source identifier. apt: repository name. winget: source name (winget/msstore). brew: tap name.
feed.title: Feed

url.description: Optional canonical URL. For 'web' sources this is the install page or download URL. For repository-based sources this is the repository URL where applicable.
url.title: Url

ItemSource.title: ItemSource

ItemStatus.description:
Outcome of a single item operation.

`up_to_date` is distinct from `success`: success means we did
something successfully; up_to_date means there was nothing to do.
The dashboard renders these differently.
ItemStatus.title: ItemStatus

Message.description:
A single human-readable log-style message.

Distinct from Python `logging` records — this is what gets persisted
in the sidecar for dashboard display, audit, and stakeholder reports.
Native scripts emit these alongside `items[]`.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at message emission. Optional.
timestamp.title: Timestamp

Message.title: Message

OperatingSystem.description:
Supported operating systems.

Tier 1 (`adapters/<os>/`): linux_ubuntu, windows, macos.
Tier 2 (`contrib/adapters/<os>/`): everything else.

The string value is what native scripts emit and what the adapter
factory uses to select an implementation.
OperatingSystem.title: OperatingSystem

Phase.description:
The 5-phase contract every category script implements.

See `docs/agents/contract.md` (Linux pre-merge) and ADR-0003 for
the contract's normative definition.

- **check**: read-only inventory of what's available. Side-effect-free.
- **plan**: enumerate exactly what would change. Side-effect-free.
- **apply**: execute changes. The only mutating phase.
- **verify**: post-apply validation. Side-effect-free.
- **cleanup**: bounded post-run housekeeping (cache prune, log rotate).
Phase.title: Phase

PhaseStatus.description:
Outcome of a phase.

`partial` is the deliberate middle ground: some items succeeded, some
failed, the phase as a whole did not abort. The orchestrator uses
this to decide whether to continue to the next phase or short-circuit.
PhaseStatus.title: PhaseStatus

id.description: UUID v4 generated at run start. Stable across all phases.
id.title: Id

dry_run.description: True if no mutations should be performed. Apply phase still runs but emits a sidecar with 'planned' items only.
dry_run.title: Dry Run

finished_at.description: ISO-8601 timestamp at run end (UTC). None until the orchestrator writes the final summary.
finished_at.title: Finished At

invocation.description: Original command-line string for human-readable audit. Optional; CLI captures this, scheduler may not.
invocation.title: Invocation

SidecarSchema.description:
Recognized sidecar schema identifiers.

The reader accepts both during the migration period. New emitters
write only `V1_ASCENDO`. See ADR-0003 for the deprecation timeline.
SidecarSchema.title: SidecarSchema

SourceType.description:
Kind of package source / feed.

`web` covers everything that's not a real package manager — direct
DMG downloads, GitHub Releases, manual installer URLs. The plugin
system is built around `web` for ad-hoc installers.
SourceType.title: SourceType

Summary.description:
Aggregate counts + headline status for a single phase sidecar.

Sums of `items[]` outcomes, plus the phase-level exit code. The
orchestrator's overall run status is computed by combining all phase
summaries — see core.orchestrator.

duration_ms.description: Total wall-clock duration for this phase, in milliseconds.
duration_ms.title: Duration Ms

exit_code.description: Phase-level exit code. 0 on full success or up-to-date; non-zero on any failure (orchestrator inspects the items[] for granular reasons).
exit_code.title: Exit Code

Summary.title: Summary

ToolInfo.description:
Identity of the tool that performed this phase.

Distinct from `HostInfo.os` because one OS may host multiple tools
(Linux can have apt + snap + flatpak + brew). Sidecars are 1:1 with
a tool execution.

name.description: Lowercase tool slug. Also used as `category` in items[].
name.title: Name

binary_path.description: Absolute path to the tool's binary (resolved at run time). Optional — useful for audit when multiple installs of the same tool exist on PATH.
binary_path.title: Binary Path

ToolInfo.title: ToolInfo

Trigger.description:
What initiated this run.

Drives audit + telemetry. Scheduled jobs are distinguished from CLI
runs because they need different default behaviors (silent mode,
automatic snapshot, no interactive confirmations).
Trigger.title: Trigger

schema.description: Schema identifier. Reader accepts both v1 variants.

category.description: Source category this sidecar describes. e.g. 'apt', 'winget'. Mirrors `tool.name` in the common case but can differ when a single tool drives multiple categories (e.g. brew → formula + cask).

items.description: Per-package operations attempted in this phase.
items.title: Items

messages.description: Phase-level log lines not associated with a specific item.
messages.title: Messages
